G8_coverage_pairs_same_moment_two_sizes_.note: The explicit 'look preserved' ask. PAIR 4/5 (close lever -> macro bar-bite) and PAIR 6/7 (macro hand-on-flute -> two-shot brushing) read STRONGLY as the same moment from two sizes. PAIR 2/3 (wide dig -> medium reaction) reads as the same scene/moment/grade from two sizes with a MINOR action variance (the medium S3 foregrounds the workman with a pick, not prominent in the wide S2) — cuts together as coverage but not a frame-exact match. ONE-FILM GRADE: consistent sepia/albumen tone and light across all 8 shots — grades as one film. The double-coverage-in-one-generation strategy works: the edit gets wide+medium / close+macro / macro+two-shot of each beat, all consistent because consistency is free inside one omni_reference generation.

notable_finding_river_context_sensitivit: Shot 1 here uses the IDENTICAL text to RUN 3 (v2.2), but the Alpheios river IS prominently present in this generation whereas it was ABSENT in RUN 3. Same Shot-1 prompt -> river present in one generation, absent in another. So the river's manifestation is CONTEXT-SENSITIVE / stochastic (the surrounding 8-shot prompt differs from v2.2's 5-shot prompt, and Shot-1 rendering depends on the whole prompt context) — it is NOT a deterministic drop from demoting the river. This moderates RUN 3's 'river absent by design' read: the river CAN appear with the camera-as-subject phrasing; RUN 3 happened to drop it. If the river is required every time, it still needs a firmer compositional anchor.
recommendation: Ships as the chapter-1 full-coverage test: the 30s/8-shot double-coverage capability is CONFIRMED. Which coverage the film uses is empirica-edit's call. videogen does not grade whether the shots cut into the final trailer — that is edit's lane.
